title: Checkpoint: After Rome
objective: After this level you can explain how Europe and the Mediterranean changed after Rome fell in the West.
summary: Rome's world passed to three heirs: western kingdoms, the Byzantine Empire and the caliphate. A timeline from 476 to 711 ties the chapter together.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: Rome’s old world ended up with three heirs.
cards.body: A West of new kingdoms, a Greek-speaking Roman East, and a caliphate reaching from Spain to the Indus. Let’s put the whole chapter on one page.

events.label: Odoacer deposes the last western emperor
Theodoric begins his rule of Italy
The hijra: Muhammad moves to Medina

cards.headline: Three heirs, one inheritance
cards.body: Historians describe Rome’s old world as passing to three heirs. In the West, kingdoms looked to the Roman Church, kings like Theodoric kept Roman government running, and monasteries copied the books. In the East, the Byzantine Empire kept Rome going behind walls that held against attackers, Arabs included, and Justinian’s code carried Roman law into the future. To the south, the caliphate took Syria and Egypt from Byzantium. A dark age? Historians rarely call it that now. A crowded one, certainly.

mascot.line: One empire, three heirs, and you just met all of them. Nicely done.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: How Rome's old world passed to three heirs: new western kingdoms, the Byzantine East and the caliphate.
Why the Byzantine Empire lasted a thousand more years, behind layered walls and with trusted gold coins.
Why monks copied books by hand, and how that kept both Christian and pagan writings alive.
Why historians now avoid the name Dark Ages, and what Sutton Hoo revealed about early England.

questions.prompt: After Rome fell in the West, which order of events is right?

options.label: Odoacer deposes the emperor, Hagia Sophia is completed, the hijra
Hagia Sophia is completed, Odoacer deposes the emperor, the hijra
The hijra, Odoacer deposes the emperor, Hagia Sophia is completed
Odoacer deposes the emperor, the hijra, Hagia Sophia is completed

questions.prompt: Of Rome’s three heirs, which one called its people Romans?

options.label: The Frankish kingdom
The Byzantine Empire
The Umayyad caliphate
options.rationale: That was a Muslim empire ruled from Damascus.

options.label: The Visigothic kingdom
options.rationale: The Visigoths were a Germanic people.

questions.explanation: The eastern empire’s people called themselves Romaioi, Romans.

questions.prompt: Why is “Dark Ages” a poor summary of the centuries after Rome fell in the West?

options.label: Nothing changed after Rome fell
Rome never really fell at all
Kingdoms, monasteries and empires kept learning and power alive
Every region went on being ruled by one empire

questions.explanation: Kingdoms, monasteries, Byzantium and the caliphate all flourished; historians now rarely use “Dark Ages”.

questions.prompt: In the early medieval West, where were most books copied?

options.label: In royal palaces, by court clerks
In city print shops
In Roman army camps
In monastery writing rooms, the scriptoria

questions.explanation: Monks copied manuscripts by hand in the scriptorium, a writing room set aside in the monastery.

questions.prompt: After Rome: the caliphs took Syria and Egypt from Byzantium. Why did Constantinople itself survive?

options.label: Its layered land walls held against attackers
The caliphs never sent armies north
options.rationale: Arab attackers did reach the walls.

options.label: It paid the caliphs with Hagia Sophia
The Franks sent an army to defend it

questions.explanation: Constantinople’s moat, outer wall and main wall held against attackers, including Arab ones.
